values.quantity: motor monitor part and electrical rating
values.value: INA228AIDGSR fixed by the owner (2026-09-30); 20-bit, 85 V bus-input rating, ±163.84 mV or ±40.96 mV shunt full scale, 312.5 nV or 78.125 nV LSB
values.refutation_tried: Recomputed the margin the line states: 85 V - 67.2 V (16 cells x 4.2 V, F15) = 17.8 V, matches exactly.

values.quantity: onboard shunt value and dissipation at 150 A
values.value: BVR-Z-R0002-1.0 (100 µΩ); at 150 A continuous: (150 A)² × 100 µΩ = 2.25 W, 150 A × 100 µΩ = 15 mV drop
values.refutation_tried: Recomputed: 150²=22,500; 22,500 × 0.0001 Ω = 2.25 W (matches); 150 × 0.0001 = 0.015 V = 15 mV (matches); 15 mV is inside the INA228's stated ±40.96 mV minimum range.

values.quantity: external shunt class and resistance range
values.value: WSBE8518L1000JKA2, busbar type, 50 to 100 µΩ, 4.5 to 9 W at 300 A
values.refutation_tried: Recomputed: at 100 µΩ, (300 A)² × 100 µΩ = 9 W (matches top of range); at 50 µΩ, 90,000 × 0.00005 Ω = 4.5 W (matches bottom of range). Both reproduce exactly.

values.quantity: alert line sharing topology (lines and node count)
values.value: critical outputs (7, one per INA3221) on one shared line, warning outputs (7) on a second shared line, both INA228 ALERTs (2) on a third shared line: 3 shared lines against 16 individually-wired outputs
values.refutation_tried: 7 INA3221 parts each contribute 1 critical + 1 warning output = 7+7=14; 2 INA228 each contribute 1 ALERT = 2; 14+2=16, matching the stated '16 individual alert outputs' and 'so 6 pins with the 3 shared lines, against 16' (6 = 3 register pins + 3 shared interrupt lines) exactly.

values.value: two 8-bit parallel-in, serial-out shift registers cascaded, latching all 16 alert nodes on one load pulse, read out over 3 main-coprocessor pins (load, clock, data)
values.refutation_tried: 2 x 8-bit = 16 bits, matching the 16-node count derived above; a load/clock/data interface is the minimum 3-pin PISO scheme and is consistent with the '6 pins' figure in the same paragraph.

values.refutation_tried: Searched IOBoard.md and Research.md's R8 row for a stated supply or pull-up voltage for the shift register or the CD4082: none found. Checked whether another voltage domain (5 V rail, display bus) reaches this circuit: no line places either part off the 3.3 V domain, but the absence of a stated figure means this is still an assumption, not a sourced requirement.

values.value: 3 CD4082 dual 4-input AND gates a board: one combines the 7 critical nodes (cascaded within the package, 4+3 real inputs), one combines the 7 warning nodes the same way, and one gate of a third combines the 2 ALERT nodes, unused inputs tied high
values.refutation_tried: A CD4082 has two 4-input AND gates; feeding one gate's output into a spare input of the second gate ANDs 4+3=7 real inputs to one output, matching the 7 critical and 7 warning node counts exactly; the 2 ALERT nodes fit one 4-input gate directly (2 tied high), leaving the package's second gate and the first cascade's spare gate unused, consistent with '3 CD4082 a board with the unused inputs tied high'.

values.quantity: existing servo current alert thresholds (A, ms)
values.value: INA3221 critical alert at 3.0 A per servo (checked every sample); warning/stall alert at 1.0 A for 400 ms
values.refutation_tried: Both figures sit below the port switch's 3.96 to 4.84 A hardware breaker floor (value below), so the software alert path is expected to act before the hardware breaker on a genuine persistent overcurrent; no numeric conflict found between the three figures.

values.quantity: port supply switch hardware breaker trip range and response time
values.value: TPS259474LRPWR circuit breaker trips at 3.96 to 4.84 A (ILIM at RILM=750 Ω); latches off after a minimal ITIMER blanking (ITIMER pin open), turn-off time tCB about 2 µs, re-arms only when EN is cycled or VIN is cycled
values.source: TI datasheet SLVSFC9C sections 6.5, 6.6, 7.3.5.2 and Table 7-3, read 2026-09-29T12:47:01Z (hardware/research/round1/FU-B1/023-P4-datasheet-R6.json, P4-confirmed); hardware/docs/Supply.md:27
values.refutation_tried: Checked the datasheet equation cited, RILM = 3334/ILIM: at RILM=750 Ω, ILIM≈4.45 A nominal, inside the stated 3.960-4.840 A band. Confirmed this part (TPS259474LRPWR, R6's port supply switch) is a different device from the R8 current monitors, so its figures only bound R8's blanking-time decision; they do not set an R8 part's own threshold.

values.quantity: INA3221 per-channel and full-cycle conversion time (ms)
values.value: 1.1 ms typical / 1.21 ms maximum per channel at CT bit=100; 3.63 ms maximum to cycle all 3 channels of one INA3221
values.source: TI INA3221 datasheet SBOS576C section 5.5, read 2026-09-29T17:20:12Z (hardware/research/round1/FU-B3/021-P4-datasheet-R8.json, P4-confirmed)
values.refutation_tried: Recomputed 1.21 ms × 3 = 3.63 ms, matches exactly. Noted CT bit=100 is the configuration round 1's P2/P4 assumed, not independently re-read in this task; if round 2 changes the INA3221's conversion-time register setting, this figure would need rereading.

values.quantity: whether the current/temperature monitors latch their ALERT outputs
values.source: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:113: "Whether the monitors latch their alert outputs is not read here."
values.refutation_tried: Checked whether the board-wide 'every stop latches' rule already answers this by extension (it is applied explicitly to the MCP9808 temperature trip, IOBoard.md:460, and to the TPS259474LRPWR port breaker, Supply.md:27, both different parts). The same paragraph that states the general case also explicitly says the monitors' own latching 'is not read here', so the general rule is not treated as deciding it for the INA3221/INA228 ALERT outputs.

values.source: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:113: "The main coprocessor acts on the critical line only when it stays low longer than a blanking time... The blanking time is not stated."
values.refutation_tried: Checked the two bounds the gap names: the port switch's near-instant 3.96-4.84 A hardware breaker (about 2 µs turn-off, value above) and the INA3221's 3.63 ms three-channel conversion cycle (value above). A blanking time must exceed 3.63 ms to see at least one full conversion of every channel, while staying well under the port breaker's response so the two layers do not race; no number between them is stated anywhere in the tree.
